title: Why you jolt awake as you fall asleep

lines.text: You're drifting off to sleep, and suddenly, you feel like you're falling. Your whole body jolts.
Around 70% of people have had one.
And about one in ten get them every single night.
It happens right at the edge of sleep, as your muscles start to relax.
Nobody knows exactly why. One theory: your brain mistakes that relaxation for actually falling.
So it jerks you awake to catch yourself.
Caffeine, stress, and being overtired can all make them more frequent.
They're harmless. Just your brain, double checking you're not falling off something.

sources.claim: About 70% of people experience hypnic jerks, about 10% daily; occur at sleep onset; often with a falling sensation; cause unknown, theories include the brain misreading relaxation as falling; triggers include caffeine, stress and fatigue
